output.brief: The rejects come from an interaction between two things, not from either one alone. Arnholt resin arrives wetter, at 0.27–0.33% moisture against 0.11–0.14% for Quillan. Dryer D5 is degraded: its dew point is −16 to −19 °C instead of −40 °C, and its alarm limit was loosened in week 31. Together they leave Arnholt resin at about 0.25–0.31% moisture at Press 5, above the 0.20% limit. That gives roughly 10% rejects. Arnholt on Press 7, whose dryer is healthy, runs at 0.8%. Quillan on D5 runs at 0.9%. The same Arnholt lot dried in a good portable dryer gave 0.8% rejects, against 10.4% through D5. The new operators are not the cause: their reject rate matches the experienced operators' on each resin. Second shift looks worse only because all of its VX runs on Press 5. The Arnholt trial missed this because it ran only on Press 7. Do not put the six operators on improvement plans. This week, repair D5 and confirm its dew point, restore the alarm limit, and keep Arnholt off D5 until then. Add a moisture check on every VX resin lot. One open question is whether the annex storage adds to the Arnholt moisture. Every Arnholt sample came from the annex, so supplier and storage can't be separated. Test that before paying for warehouse space. I'm fairly confident in the main finding.
